requirements.statement: The handler reads the optional `name` field and returns a greeting.

findings.title: REQ-TRIAGE-007 fully implemented and tested

source_anchors.excerpt: The handler reads the optional `name` field and returns a greeting.

findings.rationale: The greet() function reads the optional 'name' field from the payload dict using dict.get with a default of 'world', and returns the formatted greeting string. This directly satisfies REQ-TRIAGE-007 (SRC-TRIAGE-007-PRD). Two tests cover both the named and default-name paths, confirming both acceptance boundaries. No requirement drift, no behavioral contract change, no failing tests. DR-006 applies: behavioral contract unchanged, tests green, no requirement drift → NO_ISSUE.

findings.title: External guidance recommends runtime payload schema validation; no local requirement establishes this

source_anchors.excerpt: External guidance recommends validating untrusted request payloads against an explicit runtime schema.
This project source does not require runtime schema validation.

findings.rationale: SRC-TRIAGE-007-EXT (external_guidance authority) recommends runtime schema validation of untrusted payloads. SRC-TRIAGE-007-PRD (product_contract authority) explicitly states no runtime schema validation is required. No local requirement is violated. Per DR-004 and domain rule UNSUPPORTED_BEST_PRACTICE_CLAIM, this cannot be elevated to CONFIRMED_ISSUE. Per DR-012, POTENTIAL_RISK with UNSUPPORTED_BEST_PRACTICE_CLAIM supported only by external guidance receives severity MEDIUM. The external guidance and project source do not conflict on a project requirement — the PRD affirmatively excludes the obligation — so no ABSTAIN is triggered.
findings.suggested_human_check: Confirm whether the greet() handler is ever called with untrusted or user-controlled input in production; if so, consider whether the external guidance warrants adopting a local requirement for input validation.
